examShortTricks: Trick 1: Fill by (n + l) rule; for equal (n + l), lower n fills first — that is why 4s (4+0) fills before 3d (3+2).
Trick 2: Hund's rule in one phrase: degenerate orbitals fill singly first, with parallel spins, before pairing.

Trick 3: Exceptional configurations are guaranteed 2-mark questions: Cr = [Ar]3d5 4s1 and Cu = [Ar]3d10 4s1 — reason: exactly half-filled and fully-filled d subshells gain extra stability (exchange energy).
Trick 4: Pauli check: no two electrons in the same orbital share all four quantum numbers — max 2 per orbital, opposite spins.
keyPoints: Aufbau: orbitals fill in increasing energy order (n + l rule).
Pauli: an orbital holds at most two electrons with opposite spins.
Hund: pairing in degenerate orbitals starts only after each has one electron.
Cr and Cu show half-filled/fully-filled d-subshell stability.
practiceQuestions: Q. Write the electronic configuration of Cr (Z = 24) and explain the exception. (3 marks) — [Ar] 3d5 4s1; half-filled d5 plus 4s1 maximises exchange energy and symmetry.
Q. Why is 4s filled before 3d? (1 mark) — lower (n + l) value: 4s has 4, 3d has 5.
